merger_description:
Aware Real Estate proposes to acquire from entities affiliated with Link Real Estate Investment Trust (**Link REIT**) a 50% indirect interest in the leasehold of 100 Market Street, which is a 10-storey office tower in the Sydney CBD (the **Property**), through the acquisition of units in a trust and shares in other related entities (the **Acquisition**). Following the Acquisition, Aware Real Estate and Link REIT will each own a 50% indirect interest in the Property.

Aware Real Estate is the property investment platform responsible for the strategic performance and management of Aware Super’s directly owned Australian property portfolio. The platform manages a diversified property portfolio across industrial, office, retail and mixed-use sectors.

Link REIT is a collective investment scheme headquartered in Hong Kong, where its units are listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. Link REIT has a property portfolio primarily focused on retail, office and logistics properties and car park spaces in Chinese Mainland, Hong Kong, Australia, Singapore and the United Kingdom.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition, given:
a. Aware Real Estate’s share of commercial office space in the
Sydney CBD and surrounding areas by floor space is
• estimated to be low and the increment arising from the
Acquisition would be small
b. there are alternative commercial office offerings in the
Sydney CBD and surrounding area.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
